subject: Trial environment options & evaluation criteria
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@omnihealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Trial environment options & evaluation criteria

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap from our discovery and a concrete proposal for the trial so your team can review and confirm. TL;DR: we recommend a VPC-controlled trial given PHI concerns, but I outline hosted and dedicated sandbox options below so you have the tradeoffs.

What we covered (high level):
- Primary goals: ingest and anonymize clinical notes, run extraction + classification flows, compare latency and token-cost against existing pipeline.
- Security constraints: PHI, customer-managed keys preferred, strict egress/VPC controls.
- Success metrics: 95th percentile < 250 ms for single-request inference (50–512 tokens), end-to-end throughput of ~20 QPS for batched inferencing, output F1 >= 0.82 on the 5 test prompts.

Trial environment options (short):
1) Hosted API (fastest onboarding)
   - Pros: immediate; no infra for you to manage; 1–2 hour setup.
   - Cons: not ideal for PHI unless redaction/proxy architecture is used; KMS can be Redwood-managed.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved infra in Redwood environment)
   - Pros: isolated GPU pool, can allocate dedicated capacity, faster than full VPC onboarding.
   - Cons: still crosses Redwood-managed network boundary; support for customer KMS is possible but requires a short SRE window.
3) VPC/private trial (recommended)
   - Pros: customer-controlled VPC peering, customer KMS/HSM, audit logs exported to your Splunk/S3. Meets PHI bar.
   - Cons: longer setup (1–3 weeks depending on approvals); we'll need IP allowlist and cert exchange.

Proposed POC scope & success criteria (please confirm):
- Functional: integration with your data pipeline (s3 -> preprocessing -> Redwood inference) for 3 core extraction tasks.
- Quality: F1 >= 0.82 across seeded prompts (we will share the eval set).
- Performance: 95th <= 250 ms single-request latency; sustained 15–25 QPS for batch size 8.
- Cost signal: cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll produce an estimate once we know batch profile).

Evaluation plan & timeline (suggested):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize environment choice + NDA/POC agreement; share onboarding docs.
- Week 1: infra setup (VPC peering, KMS), sample payload tests, smoke tests.
- Week 2: run eval harness (quality+latency), iterate prompts/config.
- Week 3: final benchmarking + handoff decision.

Owners:
- Redwood PM/PD: Karthik Iyer (trial lead)
- Redwood Security: Neha Kapoor (compliance onboarding)
- Redwood Ops: Marissa Cole (SRE/infra ops)
- OmniHealth: Samantha Reed (product lead), Aaron Patel (DevOps)

Attachments: redwood_trial_guide.pdf (onboarding checklist), trial-config.yaml (example runtime config).

Next steps / asks for OmniHealth:
1) Confirm preferred environment (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC).
2) If VPC: share primary security contact + preferred start week + IP ranges/cert contact.
3) Confirm whether a 2- or 3-week trial window is preferred (we can extend to 3 weeks).
4) Share an NDA/POC ordering contact for DocuSign if procurement needs it.

Proposed onboarding call: 2026-11-17 10:00am PT — does that work for Samantha/Aaron?

Thanks — happy to adjust.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Karthik — very thorough. Quick responses from our side: 

- We are leaning strongly toward the VPC/private trial because the data will contain PHI and our legal team prefers customer-managed keys.
- A few clarifying questions: does the VPC option support integrating our HSM (we use AWS KMS with custom HSM-backed CMKs)? Also, will logs be routed to our Splunk instance?
- Procurement: Ben will need a short SOW/NDA and typically asks for a 3-week window for trials that touch PHI. Will Redwood accommodate a 3-week POC?

We'd like Aaron (DevOps) to be looped for the network and cert exchange. Can you provide a sample of the network diagram and a minimal allowlist?

Also — can you share a short checklist of what we need to prepare on our side before the onboarding call?

Onboarding call: 2026-11-17 10:00am PT works for me; Aaron and Ben will try to join.

Best,
Samantha

Subject: Re: Trial environment options & evaluation criteria — security notes

Hi Samantha / Aaron / Ben —

Thanks for confirming the call. A few security-focused answers ahead of the meeting: 

1) KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for the VPC/private deployment. We can integrate with AWS KMS CMKs; if you require FIPS/HSM-backed keys we support that via our HSM passthrough configuration (we'll need the key policy and the principal to add).

2) Logging & audit: We can stream audit logs to your S3 or Splunk instance; typical retention during POC is 30 days but we can adjust. Logs can be exported in JSON lines with structured event ids for tracing.

3) Network: We'll need an allowlist (IP ranges) and an X.509 cert exchange for VPC peering or private link. Minimal initial allowlist: 3 outbound CIDR ranges (we'll provide specifics in the onboarding doc).

4) PHI handling: We recommend an initial redaction pass at ingestion and then compare with an unredacted flow for evaluation. We'll provide a redaction utility as part of the trial (see security-faq.pdf attached).

5) Timeline: Redwood can accommodate a 3-week POC if procurement requires it. Proposed adjusted timeline: 
   - Week 0 (prep): finalize SOW/NDA + network/cert exchange
   - Week 1 (setup): VPC peering, KMS validation, smoke tests
   - Week 2 (eval): run quality and latency harness; iterate prompts
   - Week 3 (benchmark): final benchmark, cost estimate, next-steps decision

I attached security-faq.pdf with more detail and a short checklist for Aaron/DevOps to prepare (IP ranges, KMS ARN, Splunk endpoint).

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: security-faq.pdf (pdf, 28 KB)

Thanks everyone — great alignment. Confirming the plan below so we can lock calendars and the SOW.

Confirmed approach: VPC/private trial (OmniHealth-managed KMS, logs to Splunk). POC window: 3 weeks. Proposed start date: 2026-11-29 (we'll schedule the infrastructure kickoff on Nov 29 and a technical onboarding call same day).

Success criteria (finalized):
- Quality: F1 >= 0.82 on the seeded eval set (we will run the eval harness and share results).
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 250 ms for 50–512 token requests under the target load.
- Throughput: sustained 15–25 QPS with batching (batch size up to 8).
- Security: customer KMS integrated, audit logs exported to your Splunk instance, no PHI stored outside VPC.
- Ops: onboarding smoke tests passed (connectivity, certs, basic inference).

Checkpoint cadence: weekly checkpoints every Friday during the POC with short status notes from both sides. Final demo + readout at the end of Week 3.

Action owners & immediate asks:
- OmniHealth: Aaron Patel — share IP allowlist + KMS ARN + Splunk endpoint by 2026-11-24. Ben Turner — SOW/NDA contact + PO contact. Samantha — confirm start date.
- Redwood: Karthik Iyer — onboarding lead & trial runbook. Marissa Cole — SRE contact for peering and cert exchange. Neha Kapoor — security validation and audit streaming.

Attachments included: redwood_trial_guide.pdf, trial-config.yaml, security-faq.pdf. Links: HubSpot deal and onboarding calendar (see related_links).

Next steps: Aaron and Ben, please confirm by EOD 2026-11-24 so we can start the network prep. Once we have the allowlist+KMS ARN we will create the temporary VPC peering request and share cert details.

Thanks — excited to get this running.
